title: Yamuna Singh Yadav @ Jamuna Yadav v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J. and Kshitij Shailendra, J.
disposition: Writ disposed as infructuous; fresh Supply Code order reserved.
headnote: Writ against an electricity recovery certificate. The licensee withdrew the final assessment for technical reasons after admitting that the prescribed procedure had not been followed. The petition was disposed of as infructuous, with liberty to pass a fresh order strictly under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Yamuna Singh Yadav, also known as Jamuna Yadav, filed a writ challenging the recovery certificate dated 31 January 2024 issued by respondent no. 4 for electricity dues. On 5 March 2024, counsel for the electricity department admitted that the prescribed procedure had not been followed in issuing the final assessment order, and the writ was directed to be connected with Writ-C No. 3458 of 2024. The Executive Engineer then stated that the final assessment, which was not happily worded, had been withdrawn on 2 March 2024 for technical reasons.

holding_units.topic: Fresh order after withdrawal of a procedurally defective final assessment
holding_units.holding: The electricity department having withdrawn the final assessment and the recovery founded on it for technical reasons, the writ challenging the recovery certificate is disposed of as infructuous. The department remains at liberty to pass a fresh order strictly in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

principle_tags.application: Applied to dispose of the writ as infructuous once the licensee withdrew the final assessment and recovery for technical reasons, while reserving liberty to pass a fresh order strictly under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

not_decided.point: Validity and quantum of any fresh assessment of the electricity dues
not_decided.note: The impugned final assessment was withdrawn by the department. The Court did not examine the dues and left the licensee free to pass a fresh order under the Supply Code procedure.
